- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — overcorrects toward historical mean; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day moving average instead.
- Model underestimates volatility in late forecast horizon (days 20–30); increase forecast variance by 5–10% for days 20+ if no event-driven sentiment shift.
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal after a spike, model fails to recognize it; add a 2–3 day lag correction for reversal events.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), avoid extrapolating from 30-day trend; use 14-day rolling average for more responsive correction.
